reasons: The action and claim directly match the source's explicit recommendation to prefer specificity over broad application on both landing pages and ads.

The source explicitly says every line of landing-page copy must pass the “so what” test by explaining why the statement matters; the candidate accurately expresses this as explaining why the line is being mentioned.
The source explicitly recommends pain-led or benefit-led rather than feature-led headlines and identifies this as one of the few landing-page elements worth split testing.
The action retains the source's required sequence: export existing reviews, submit them to an LLM, and ask for unique feedback that differentiates the product.
The candidate appropriately notes that the source does not guarantee useful output or prescribe a particular model or export method.
The source presents tactical combination of multiple benefits as an option for creating differentiated positioning.

The exclusions accurately preserve the source's caveat that merely stringing together arbitrary benefits is insufficient and that free shipping, service, and delivery are treated as baseline expectations rather than differentiators.
The candidate accurately presents this as an attributed example rather than general implementation guidance.
It retains the speaker's uncertainty about the Bloom example and does not assert that the formula itself was differentiated.

The source explicitly recommends repositioning into white space, describes purple ocean as another framing, and explains marketing-based repositioning of a commoditized product without necessarily changing the product.
The candidate does not invent a method for finding white space and correctly identifies that the source lacks one.

omissions.description: The source separately recommends reading Blue Ocean Strategy in connection with the repositioning concept; this recommendation is not represented by the candidates or unchanged context.
omissions.quote: I would recommend going and reading uh Blue Ocean Strategy.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-thought, so preceding context for the initial above-the-fold discussion is unavailable.
The excerpt ends during the Bloom example, so any qualification or conclusion following the statement that the product was effectively the same is unavailable.

Claims about conversion, consumer trust, CAC, market share, and positioning effectiveness are presented as the speaker's assertions; the excerpt supplies no study design, measurements, numerical results, or validation criteria.
The source provides limited operational detail for selecting personas, angles, complementary benefits, or white-space opportunities.
